blocks.text: Imagine you have a series of tasks, each with a start and end time, and you want to complete as many as possible without overlap. How do you choose which tasks to perform? This is the essence of interval scheduling.

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore greedy algorithms for interval scheduling and Huffman coding. Greedy algorithms make locally optimal choices at each step with the hope of finding a global optimum. We will see how these principles apply to scheduling tasks and constructing optimal prefix codes.

blocks.title: Interval Scheduling Problem
blocks.text: Given a set of intervals, each with a start and end time, the goal is to select the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.

blocks.markdown: To solve the interval scheduling problem using a greedy algorithm, we must choose the correct criterion. The key insight is to always select the interval that ends the earliest, as this leaves the most room for subsequent intervals.

blocks.caption: Set of intervals where $s_i$ is the start time and $f_i$ is the end time of interval $i$.

blocks.title: Interval Scheduling Example
blocks.prompt: Consider intervals: (1, 4), (3, 5), (0, 6), (5, 7), (3, 8), (5, 9), (6, 10), (8, 11), (8, 12), (2, 13), (12, 14). Select the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.

steps.text: 3. Select the next interval that starts after 4, which is (5, 7).

blocks.title: Greedy Criterion for Interval Scheduling
blocks.text: Always select the interval with the earliest end time that is compatible with the already selected intervals.

blocks.markdown: Next, we explore Huffman coding, a method to construct optimal prefix codes based on the frequencies of symbols. This is crucial in data compression, where we aim to minimize the total length of encoded data.

blocks.title: Huffman Coding
blocks.text: A method of encoding symbols such that the most frequent symbols use the shortest codes, resulting in an optimal prefix code.

blocks.title: Huffman Coding Example
blocks.prompt: Given symbol frequencies: A: 45, B: 13, C: 12, D: 16, E: 9, F: 5. Construct the Huffman code.

steps.text: 1. Create a leaf node for each symbol and build a priority queue based on frequencies.
2. Extract two nodes with the lowest frequency: F (5) and E (9). Merge them into a new node with frequency 14.
3. Repeat: Merge nodes C (12) and the new node (14) into a node with frequency 26.
4. Merge nodes B (13) and D (16) into a node with frequency 29.
5. Merge nodes with frequencies 26 and 29 into a node with frequency 55.
6. Merge the last two nodes: A (45) and the node with frequency 55 into the root node with frequency 100.

blocks.answer: The Huffman codes are: A: 0, B: 101, C: 1000, D: 111, E: 10011, F: 10010.

blocks.caption: Huffman codes for given symbol frequencies.

blocks.markdown: Huffman coding guarantees an optimal prefix code because it builds the code tree in a bottom-up manner, ensuring that the most frequent symbols have the shortest codes.

blocks.title: Optimality of Huffman Coding
blocks.text: Huffman coding is optimal because it minimizes the weighted path length of the code tree, which corresponds to the expected length of the encoded data.

points: Interval scheduling can be solved using a greedy algorithm by selecting intervals with the earliest end time.
Huffman coding constructs an optimal prefix code by assigning shorter codes to more frequent symbols.
